title: Space Hamlet – Cockpit, London
summary: A review of Space Hamlet at the Cockpit in London, a stage reworking of Shakespeare's Hamlet, which is on the 2027 session. The text is short, but it may be useful for Yamuna's seconde and première teaching and for thinking about adaptation.

title: The Student Exchange Program That Never Leaves the U.S.
summary: An article on a student exchange scheme that keeps students within the United States, drawing on Saskia Sassen's idea that culture is not bounded by national borders. It may interest you as a teacher thinking about education and mobility.

title: Grenoble : 100 rendez-vous pour réparer et consommer autrement
summary: Economie Matin lists around 100 events in Grenoble for repairing things and consuming differently, such as repair cafés. The text gives no dates, but it fits local life well.

title: Are You With Me Now? by Hanif Kureishi review – a novelist unleashed
summary: A review of Hanif Kureishi's Are You With Me Now?, written after a devastating accident left him tetraplegic. The reviewer finds his restricted life gives his narration a new, thrilling immediacy, rebellious and vivid.

title: Surveillance and sabotage on the Deutsche Börse photography prize shortlist – in pictures
summary: Pictures from the Deutsche Börse photography prize shortlist, marking its 30th anniversary. The nominees explore hidden human labour, life in wartime Ukraine and the Buddhist concept of rebirth, offering a good visual essay on contemporary photography.

title: Smartphones, ancient tracking skills and a future for desert lions
summary: Rangers in Namibia are combining real-time data and smartphones with traditional tracking skills to help farmers and protect a recovering desert lion population. It is a hopeful conservation story that shows local knowledge working alongside modern tools.

title: Pontcharra. L’exposition des 25 ans d’Art’M est visible jusqu’au 6 novembre
summary: Until 6 November 2026 in Pontcharra, Art'M celebrates 25 years with an exhibition. Pontcharra lies in the Grésivaudan valley near Les Adrets, and the anniversary of a local arts group is a warm, community-rooted story.

title: Toussaint à Grenoble : 9 sorties pour ce week-end du 30 octobre au 1er novembre, de la Foire aux ateliers créatifs
summary: Grenoble, 30 October to 1 November 2026: a roundup of nine outings for the Toussaint weekend, including a fair of creative workshops. The text is only a headline, so the details of each outing are not available here.

title: Reinventing fairy tales for the 21st century
summary: A BBC Front Row discussion of how fairy tales are being reinvented and subverted for today, including Daniel Foxx's satirical book on privileged children. It is strongly literary and well suited to your love of story and narrative voice.

title: Netflix’s New 4-Part Thriller Turns A Dream Getaway Into A Nightmare This Friday
summary: A four-part Netflix thriller premiering this Friday, 31 October, in which a dream getaway turns into a nightmare. The text is only a headline, but it fits her taste for thrillers.

title: Spotlight on Lauren Cuthbertson #Ballet #RoyalBalletAndOpera
summary: A Royal Ballet video in which Lauren Cuthbertson recalls learning Juliet from Monica Mason in MacMillan's Romeo and Juliet and the value of passing knowledge between generations. World Ballet Day streamed on 29 October, so the live event has passed, but the video remains available.

title: Nature-Inspired Tech Prevents Microplastics Entering Atlantic Ocean Through Wastewater
summary: Princeton alumni have built a device, inspired by water-repellent plants, that filters microplastics from wastewater, and it is already in use in Atlantic City. It is a concrete environmental step that stops plastics reaching the Atlantic.

title: "I Wish I Could Write a Love Story Free from History"... South African Novelist Damon Galgut's Unfinished Questions
summary: South African novelist Damon Galgut reflects on writing a love story free from history and on the questions his fiction leaves open. It speaks directly to how novels carry history, which is central to your reading interests.

title: An introduction to The Royal Ballet's Manon
summary: An introduction from the Royal Ballet to Kenneth MacMillan's Manon, a devastating ballet set in 18th-century Paris about a woman torn between love and wealth. Ideal for a dance-loving reader who enjoys strong characters and dramatic storytelling.

title: Skulls, bulls and someone peeing in her own eye: four great exhibitions to see for free
summary: A Guardian roundup of four free exhibitions, including Andy Warhol's skulls and Pierre Bonnard's fruit, which the piece argues have more in common than expected. It is a useful guide to art you can see without paying.

title: Their orchestra is not a sacred object but a tool for struggle – Paris’s musicians join the frontline
summary: The Paris orchestra L'Orchestre du Nouveau Monde gained attention for playing through tear gas during last week's student protests. The piece also places the group within a tradition of radical orchestras. It is strongest as a classical-music story, and the protest context is secondary.

title: Our Fall Issue Cover: Elizabeth Glaessner’s Big Head
summary: The Paris Review's fall issue cover, Elizabeth Glaessner's painting Big Head, with the editors noting that its title teases a tiny figure painting a giant head. It links a painting directly to a literary magazine, which may appeal to Yamuna's interest in art and writing.

title: Bizarre Rescue Sees Divers Save Kangaroo That Found Itself Over a Mile from Dry Land
summary: A scuba diver and his crew rescued a juvenile kangaroo that had swum more than a mile and a half out to sea, spotted first by the captain in Boston Bay, South Australia. It is a light, charming animal rescue story.

title: La Mire du 28 octobre
summary: A TV zapping round-up for 28 October covering Israeli elections, Mbappé's second place in the Ballon d'Or and a government plan to restrict social networks. It also asks whether we are all addicted to screens, a question that may interest a teacher.

title: Stranger Anonymously Pays $420 Lunch Tab for 27 Disabled Residents and Caregivers
summary: A stranger anonymously paid a $420 barbecue lunch for 27 staff and disabled residents of a community centre in Incheon, near Seoul. A small, warm act of kindness with a concrete outcome.

title: 'Renoir was absolutely fascinated by love'💕|#SHORTS | National Gallery
summary: A short National Gallery video in which curators Christopher Riopelle and Chiara Di Stefano discuss Renoir's paintings of friends, family and lovers, linked to the 'Renoir and Love' exhibition. It is a brief, accessible way into his warmer, more intimate work.

title: La Mire du 27 octobre
summary: The 27 October 2026 TV roundup. Its main items are Lula's historic victory in Brazil, a shooting and an attack in the Yvelines, and political disputes over racism. It is mostly hard news.

title: Who will win The Booker Prize?
summary: An 11-minute BBC Radio 4 Open Book episode in which Simon Savidge goes through the Booker shortlist book by book and says who he thinks will win and who should. It suits a reader who enjoys thoughtful, book-by-book talk about contemporary fiction.

title: Audrey Niffenegger on the sequel to her hugely successful novel The Time Traveller's Wife
summary: Audrey Niffenegger discusses Life Out of Order, the sequel to The Time Traveller's Wife, returning to the time-travelling father and daughter. The same episode also covers Kyle MacLachlan's memoir and a segment on Dracula's long literary history, all strongly suited to her.

title: La Mire du 26 octobre
summary: The 26 October 2026 TV roundup. It mentions Halloween theme parks selling out and the enduring fascination with zombies, alongside coverage of an attack in Trappes and a march in Aubervilliers.

title: Dances at a Gathering –  Yasmine  Naghdi and William Bracewell
summary: A Royal Ballet and Opera clip of Yasmine Naghdi and William Bracewell dancing the Apricot and Green pas de deux from Jerome Robbins's Dances at a Gathering, set to Chopin. It returns to the Main Stage in London from 9 to 28 November.

title: La Mire du 25 octobre
summary: The 25 October 2026 TV roundup. It reports on protests, with police figures of 410,000 participants, and the Interior Minister's comments. It also notes a tennis qualifier at the Open de France.

title: A birthday with a fanfare 🎺 Carmen overture #Bizet #RoyalBalletAndOpera
summary: On World Opera Day and Bizet's birthday, the Royal Opera posted the overture to Carmen. The production returns to the Main Stage from 29 October, so this is a lively way to hear the score before a visit.

title: Behind every mask lies a secret 🎭  A Masked Ball (Philipp Stölzl)
summary: A video introducing Philipp Stölzl's new production of Verdi's A Masked Ball, his Royal Opera debut, with forbidden love, conspiracy and revenge at its core. It runs on the Main Stage from 30 November to 18 December.
